text:
anika-partnerships: Heads up — during SI onboarding we discovered the partner's committed delivery lead times don't line up with the marketplace commit window. They quoted 18–28 days from PO to rack-ready, marketplace commit assumes 14 days. We need to decide on a buffer and whether to relax the commit window for this partner.
ryan-procurement: Ouch. Partner contract language had 'target lead time 3 weeks' but their recent run shows spikes to 4 weeks. We should add explicit buffer days and update the commit calendar.
kevin-sales: This will impact a couple of sales cycles in EMEA if we push the commit. Customers expect start-of-quarter availability. Can we do a partial commit? e.g., firm reserve for baseline capacity + option to scale later? :thinking_face:
mia-logistics: If freight is the blocker we can prioritize air for the first wave but it's +$ per unit. Also need lead time for customs paperwork — that's another ~3 business days variability.
devon-ops: From an infra perspective we can stage less than full rack in region and use routing policies to spread risk. But that increases complexity for Dedicated onboarding and pushback from customers wanting contiguous capacity.
anika-partnerships: Good notes. Two parallel asks: (1) commercial: negotiate explicit buffer & an optional air-lift for M1 customers; (2) product/ops: define graceful degraded allocation so we can ship partial capacity without breaking contracts.
ryan-procurement: Proposed buffer: 10 days on top of partner lead time, so marketplace commit window = partner ETA + 10. That gets us to ~28–38 days worst case, which is heavy. Alternative: split commit tiers: Tier A (firm 14d) requires partner to guarantee air-lift SLA; Tier B (30d) standard.
kevin-sales: Tiering makes sense. We can offer Tier A as a premium add-on to customers who need strict Q-start. Need pricing delta.
mia-logistics: To operationalize Tier A we need a hold at port and dedicated customs broker. That adds ~2–4 days but reduces variability.
devon-ops: For degraded allocation, here's a quick config snippet we can use in rollout policy:
```yaml
allocation_policy:
  primary_region: eu-west-1
  fallback_regions: [us-east-1, ap-southeast-1]
  minimum_contiguous_racks: 0  # allow partial
  notify_on_partial: true
```
This lets us accept partial rack deliveries and route by policy.
anika-partnerships: Nice. Action items: (a) @ryan-procurement to reopen SLAs with partner and propose Tier A/B structure + air-lift pricing, (b) @mia-logistics to cost customs/air-lift ops for Tier A, (c) @devon-ops to prototype allocation_policy by EOD Fri, (d) @kevin-sales to draft customer messaging and pricing delta.
ryan-procurement: I'll ping supplier today. My ask: partner needs to sign addendum for Tier A SLAs (air-lift commitment + penalties). I'll share draft by tomorrow.
kevin-sales: I'll draft a short two-line email and a follow-up FAQs doc for customers who ask about start-window.
mia-logistics: I'll model two options and post cost delta as a table in this thread.
devon-ops: Will push a branch with the rollout policy and a small simulator to validate latency impacts if we split racks across regions.
anika-partnerships: If partner refuses Tier A, we either widen marketplace commit window or pause bringing them into the marketplace for Dedicated commitments. Not ideal but necessary to protect SLOs. :warning:
orion-bot: Reminder — calendar event created: "Partner SLA sync: supplier X" Tue 10:00 UTC (invites: anika-partnerships, ryan-procurement, mia-logistics, kevin-sales, devon-ops).
kevin-sales: Thanks @orion-bot. Also FYI — a customer in APAC asked for an on-prem option; we should surface cost of Tier A vs on-prem onboarding.
anika-partnerships: Great. Let's reconvene after ryan shares supplier response. Keep updates short. :eyes:
